statement_en: Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes $a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
noncomputable def intPartialDensity (S : Set ℤ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (((Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) (N : ℤ)).filter (fun m => m ∈ S)).card : ℝ) /
    (2 * (N : ℝ) + 1)
end Set

namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
def HasIntDensity (S : Set ℤ) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => S.intPartialDensity N) atTop (𝓝 α)
end Set

open Filter Topology

def ResidueChoice (n : ℕ → ℕ) := ∀ i : ℕ, ZMod (n i)

def avoidAll (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

def avoidPrefix (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) (k : ℕ) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, i < k → (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

theorem erdos_97054 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε := by
  sorry
